sections.name: discoverIndustryNews
sections.title: Read Bing News results
sections.what: Requests the Bing News feed for a query, reads up to eight items, unwraps Bing redirects to the publisher's address, keeps only web addresses, and returns each item's address, title, and publish date text. It throws if the feed is unavailable and always closes the parser.
sections.why: The comment says the results are discovery only; the code keeps the feed's leads separate from proof.
sections.watch_out: The redirect unwrap depends on Bing's current feed format, so a format change can silently return fewer or no results.

summary: Searches a public Bing News feed for a query and returns up to eight article links to use as leads for further research.
purpose: Add news leads to research without treating search snippets as proof.
why: The comment says the feed supplements configured providers and that its snippets are discovery, not evidence. The redirect unwrapping is explained in the code: Bing's feed carries the publisher's real address inside its redirect link.
how: 1. Request the RSS feed for the query. 2. Parse the XML. 3. Take up to eight items. 4. For each item, read the link, unwrap any Bing redirect, keep only web addresses, and read the title and publish date text. 5. Close the parser whether or not it succeeded.
outputs: A list of objects with url, title, and publishedAt (raw date text, which may be missing).
risks: Depends on Bing's RSS format and its redirect parameter name; a change could return nothing without an error. Publish dates are kept as raw text and not checked. The function throws when the feed is unavailable, so every caller must handle that.
debug: If results are empty, open the feed address in a browser and check the query. If the error says the news feed is unavailable, check connectivity or the provider's status. If links look like Bing addresses, check whether the redirect parameter name has changed.
